candidates.core_provocation: A paid companion is hired by a stranger with early dementia to spend one afternoon pretending to be his daughter. He gives her a key and insists she must help him correct a terrible mistake, but each time he remembers what happened, the story changes.
candidates.why_interesting: The reader must keep questioning whether the stranger is revealing a real crime, confusing the past, or testing the one person who might believe him.

candidates.core_provocation: After a minor train accident, two strangers are asked to make a joint memory record because no camera captured what happened. Both remember saving the same missing child—and each remembers the other taking the child away.
candidates.why_interesting: Conflicting memories turn two ordinary strangers into possible witnesses, suspects, and each other’s only hope of finding the child.

candidates.core_provocation: A stranger pays the narrator to memorize a confession and keep it only in her head while he undergoes surgery that may erase his memory. When he wakes and says he has never seen her, she must decide whether a confession still belongs to someone who no longer remembers making it.
candidates.why_interesting: It creates immediate tension around a dangerous secret while asking a surprising question about responsibility and memory.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first idea offers the clearest short-story engine: one afternoon, two strangers, a key, and a series of changing revelations. It combines emotional awkwardness with growing suspense while keeping the truth of the memory genuinely uncertain until the end.
